post.description:
Exchange a verified bearer token for the user's tenant context.

Verifies the token (Firebase ID token or dev token), confirms the user is
provisioned + active and the tenant is not suspended, lazily backfills the
Firebase UID / custom claims on first sign-in, and returns session metadata.

Local dev-only login. Returns a short-lived dev identity token.

Disabled whenever Firebase is configured (and therefore always disabled in
production, which requires Firebase).

Start a session for the shared public demo account — server-side.

The marketing site's "Try the Sandbox" button calls this with no body. The
backend looks up the configured demo tenant/user and mints a token for it
(a dev token in dev mode, a Firebase custom token in Firebase mode). No
password is ever sent to or from the browser, so nothing secret ships in the
client bundle.

Revoke the caller's Firebase refresh tokens (real mode) and audit.

Relies on ``TenantContextMiddleware`` having already verified the bearer and
populated ``request.state``.

Create a new tenant and user.

If Firebase is enabled, also registers the user in Firebase Auth and sets custom claims.

schema.title: Response Signup Api V1 Auth Signup Post

post.description:
Provision a new SANKET tenant + user for a first-time Google sign-in.

Verifies the Firebase ID token, creates the Tenant + User (no password),
links the firebase_uid, sets custom claims, and returns SessionInfo so the
SPA can complete the login without a second round-trip.

Only available when Firebase is enabled (i.e. never in dev-fallback mode).

Redeem an invitation and join its workspace.

Public, because the invitee has no bearer yet -- ``routers/invites.py`` has
always minted a link to ``/accept-invite?token=...`` and nothing has ever
redeemed it.

Everything that decides privilege is read from the invite row: which
workspace, which role, and (via the workspace) which industry. The request
supplies only the invitee's own name and password. Extra fields in the body
are ignored, so an attacker cannot promote themselves by adding ``role``.

The token is compared by SHA-256 hash, matching how ``POST /invites`` stored
it. A single-use check, an expiry check and a seat re-check all run here
rather than only at invite time, because all three can change in the days
between sending a link and someone clicking it.

get.description:
Every industry SANKET supports. Public.

Public because the signup form needs the canonical list before the caller
has a token, and because prospects may legitimately browse every vertical.
It replaces an authenticated ``/industry/available``, which enumerated all
five to someone already inside a workspace -- a list they cannot act on and
should not be shown, since they have exactly one industry.

The list comes from the backend registry, so a frontend picker cannot drift
from the codes the API will actually accept.

post.description:
Correct the workspace's industry during initial setup.

This is no longer a switch. A workspace is scoped to one industry, and this
endpoint exists only so an owner who picked the wrong one at signup can fix
it before the choice starts mattering. It closes for good once setup
completes or real data arrives (:func:`_lock_reason`), and returns 409 after
that -- a later change needs a deliberate, support-assisted migration, not
an API call that silently reinterprets existing data.

Re-minting the token
--------------------
``ind`` is baked into the bearer at login and read straight off the claim by
``TenantContextMiddleware``. Writing the database without reissuing the
token left the rest of the session running on the old industry -- for a
pharma tenant that meant a 26-week horizon, fashion signals and standard
audit level behind a header rendering "GXP - 21 CFR PART 11"
(docs/audit/02 P0-4). The first session is when a tenant runs their baseline
forecast, so the window was small and badly placed.

Because this is now the *only* writer of ``tenants.industry``, the staleness
window is closed rather than merely narrow: dev mode gets a re-minted
bearer, and Firebase mode gets fresh custom claims plus a refresh-token
revocation, so the superseded ``ind`` cannot be replayed for the remaining
hour of the old ID token's life.

get.description:
KPI cards for today / this week / this month / this year.

Each bucket reports units, gross & net revenue, returns and transaction
count, plus a revenue delta vs the equal elapsed slice of the prior period.

Computation: one aggregate query per (period, window). These are kept as
*narrow-window* scans on purpose — benchmarking showed that collapsing them
into a single ``SUM(...) FILTER (...)`` query is ~1.5x SLOWER, because the
single query must scan the whole ``[year_prior_start, now)`` union and apply
every filter per row, whereas the windowed queries each touch only their own
(mostly tiny: today / week / month) slice. The real latency win here is the
response cache wrapping this producer — repeated dashboard polls are served
from Redis in well under a millisecond instead of re-aggregating. See
docs/PERFORMANCE.md and benchmarks/bench_sales_summary.py.

Token-authenticated canonical sale-event ingest for the rest_api /
webhooks connectors.

Auth: send the push token from the connect step as ``X-Sanket-Token: <token>``
or ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``. The token's SHA-256 resolves the
tenant + connection, so this endpoint is public (no session cookie/JWT).

Body (single object, ``{"events": [...]}``, or a JSON array) of canonical
events::

    {"sku": "SKU001", "quantity": 2, "revenue": 2500,
     "timestamp": "2026-06-15T14:20:00Z", "channel": "pos"}

get.description:
Minimal liveness probe for load balancer health checks.

Returns liveness plus `git_sha`, the commit this build was produced
from. The SHA is here rather than only on /health/detailed so that a
deploy smoke test, a CI job, or a human with curl can confirm what is
actually running without needing a token — the gap that let two rounds
of payment fixes be reviewed as "shipped" while the running build
predated all of them.

Everything else (version, environment, per-subsystem status) stays
behind /health/detailed. Note the tradeoff: a commit SHA fingerprints
the exact build. That is the point, and it is also disclosure. Move
this line to /health/detailed if you would rather not publish it.

AcceptInviteRequest.title: AcceptInviteRequest
AcceptInviteRequest.description:
Redeem a one-time invite link.

Deliberately accepts no workspace, no role and no industry. All three come
from the invite record an owner or admin created; a client able to name its
own role would be a plain privilege-escalation path, and one able to name
its own industry would defeat the point of scoping a workspace at all.

``extra="forbid"`` rather than Pydantic's default ignore: a request that
tries to send ``role`` should be told it is wrong, not silently obeyed in
part. The guarantee no longer rests on a default staying put.

SandboxSessionResponse.title: SandboxSessionResponse
SandboxSessionResponse.description:
Server-side response for the public demo sandbox.

Two shapes, distinguished by ``mode``:
* ``dev``  — ``access_token`` is a short-lived dev identity token the SPA
  uses as a bearer directly (Firebase not configured).
* ``firebase`` — ``custom_token`` is a Firebase custom token the SPA
  exchanges for an ID token via ``signInWithCustomToken``.

No password is ever involved, so nothing secret reaches the browser.

SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo
SessionInfo.description:
Identity + tenant context returned to the client after authentication.

The bearer token itself is a Firebase ID token (prod) or a dev token
(local); this payload only carries the non-secret session metadata the SPA
needs to render.
